title: Copied-information floor of the selected centre path
body:
# Copied-information floor of the selected centre path (`centre-path-sharing`)

## Scope

Drawn card: `centre-path-sharing` (track `recursive-interfaces`, scope key `a55534776f5479f1686c`), drawn by `scripts/choose_research_task.py` with seed `3eca9612dd994cf5cbf01134bb839c3d` at priority revision 6, base `997e6a9ca7b4f95d50e366f61412fd640d72a88a`. The draw returned three cards: `centre-path-sharing`, `joint-query-controller`, `coverage-law-change`. No re-draw was needed. `scope_status` is `unchanged` and `actual_scope` equals the card question, byte-equal `original_card` in [TASK.json](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/research/agent-90-centre-demand-a5553477-3eca9612/research/centre-demand-rank-floor/TASK.json).

Saturation handling was kept inside the card. The card's method 1 (fully charged k-call sharing relaxation) is saturated by [PR 3075](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3075) (Aaron Wang), which priced k = 2, 4, 8, 16 windows with restoration, hosting and precision charged. This package takes the unsaturated hard-search reading of method 2 at its smallest instance: prove a lower bound on copied information per call for the selected decoder contract.

The question is the card's: can the 64-per-call centre path (eight rank-8 COPY/ERASE totals through the private temporary) be shared across calls or shrunk? Package: `research/centre-demand-rank-floor/`.

## Result 1: the eight totals are demand-independent (exact)

Recomputed from one frozen member of the selected replay archive, `candidate/strict/global/base/split-centres/GLOBAL-TEMPLATE.json.gz` in `research/community-frontier1094-audit/selected-replay.tar.gz`, both orientations:

- the centre phase is 256 macros, eight blocks of 32: one CLEAR of private scratch `C_k`, one COPY/ERASE total, one rank-8 `center` ascent at frame `414+k`, and 28 fanout (forward) or gather (backward) events at coefficients `+1/4` or `-1/4`;
- the eight source rows are `S = (229, 224, 227, 225, 243, 241, 259, 257)`, scratch `C_0..C_7` in the private namespace `[23408, 23416)`, consumer rows exactly `112..223`;
- the `112 x 8` consumer demand matrix `D` (row `r`, column `k` = coefficient of total `k` in consumer row `r`) has exact rational rank `8`, with the explicit nonzero minor on rows `(112, 117, 118, 120, 113, 116, 115, 123)` of determinant exactly `-1/16384` (that is `-1` after scaling by `4^8`);
- the backward gather matrix equals the forward fanout matrix entry for entry.

Consequence: the pinned consumer endpoint determines all eight totals independently. Any replacement copied-total contract delivering the same endpoint must move at least eight independent scalar totals per call. With the per-total pairing-rank floor of eight for root-code factors (the `64 rank(C)` package [research/p112-batch-centre-floor](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/tree/main/research/p112-batch-centre-floor), whose one-call census and factor-linear floor are credited below), the charged `8 x 8 = 64` per call is rank-forced. The centre path cannot be **shrunk** under the pinned endpoint. The lever table's favourable relaxations ("centre path free" 2.80x, "shared by two calls" 1.90x in `research/complex-local-word-ceiling`) assume away charges the pinned contract's demand forces.

## Result 2: the sharing half at demand level, and the recorded physical datum

The 144 selected calls (80 forward, 64 backward, 16 per stage over nine stages) each carry their own centre block in call-local space, and the pinned replica lift declares a direct-sum instantiation ("direct sum of data and dedicated banks; share only restored private streams"). For any k-call window the requested matrix is block diagonal in disjoint variables, so the coupling matrix is `C = I_k` and the `64 rank(C)` law of `research/p112-batch-centre-floor` gives the floor `64k`. Sharing one centre path across calls is admissible only when the consumer requests a lower-rank combination; the pinned two-panel shared-sink contract is exactly the all-ones case, where both panels request the image of the sum, a different endpoint as that package records.

The remaining datum is physical: which calls, if any, literally share sink rows, return operator and chart within one uninterrupted window. It is not decodable from the pinned owner nominations, which carry the centre source rows in only 16 of 1,152 lookups; the data-row instantiation lives in `route_semantics` (`cover class d*rho(stage,port)`). No eligible pair is exhibited and none is excluded physically; the exact missing map is named in TASK.json's open questions.

## Acceptance-gate statement

There is no changed charge or copy profile to price: the profile stays eight rank-8 totals per call and the comparison ceiling is the unchanged baseline `a < 0.001690054109089`, reproduced by the card's own positive control, run as a registered command. Restoration, hosting and precision charges can only make the unchanged profile more expensive, never cheaper, so the floor needs none of them.

## Verification

Registered replay (`python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/centre-demand-rank-floor`), verbatim output lines:

```text
PASS_CENTRE_DEMAND_RANK_FLOOR demand_rank 8 totals 8 consumer_rows 112 minor_det -1/16384 calls 144 owner_lookups_missing 1136 no_new_kappa
PASS_COMPLEX_LOCAL_WORD_CEILING a_ceiling 0.00169005410908900006 kappa<= 0.0016872026453254019
PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE research/centre-demand-rank-floor outcome=completed
```

Metadata and byte checks, verbatim:

```text
PASS_PACKAGE_METADATA_AND_PINS (not a mathematical acceptance check)
PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES {"commit": "6e36982ccc888bdb4dc15982322d8fe1aed392b4", "files": 7, "package": "research/centre-demand-rank-floor"}
```

Four rejection controls are enforced in the verifier: a zeroed demand column and a merged column pair each drop the rank below eight, a fanout sign flip fails gather equality, and a source-row swap fails the pinned source tuple. `RESULT.json` must equal the recomputation byte for byte. All arithmetic is exact (rational); the rank is recomputed by elimination and by the pinned minor.

## Scope and limits

- The floor holds for the pinned selected decoder contract and its literal consumer endpoint. Changed endpoints, changed alphabets and outside-code factors are outside it.
- The per-total pairing-rank-eight factor is inherited from `research/p112-batch-centre-floor` (credited); this package does not reprove it and does not price outside-code terms.
- The demand rank is a linear-information statement at the consumer, not a physical circuit, tape, precision or hosting claim. No selected cold replay is run; the frozen archive is read-only.
- No kappa, supplier admission, eligible window or frontier change is claimed. The selected record, frozen archives and upstream are unchanged.

## Credit

Packing-ceiling model, lever table and coverage identity: Douglas Colkitt, `research/complex-local-word-ceiling` and [PR 1012](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1012) (thakrarsagar). Coupling-rank law and `64 rank(C)` floor: `research/p112-batch-centre-floor`, prepared for alephnan with OpenAI Codex assistance; its one-call support census is credited there to [PR 845](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/845) (mihir-s-05), independently corroborated by [PR 1098](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1098) (Adam Gall), and its one-call factor-linear floor to [PR 1180](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1180) (woklerx). Pinned two-panel shared-sink contract: ToikY, `research/centre-shared-return-guard`, built on [PR 1708](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1708) (Cinna Davis / 1337isnot1337) and [PR 1748](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1748) (ToikY). k-call charged relaxation: [PR 3075](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3075) (Aaron Wang). Selected construction: [PR 1094](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1094) (rohanarun) and the lineage in the selected record.

Prepared by Aaron Wang with help from opencode (substantial AI assistance; no model named; no independent human review claimed). New work is Apache-2.0.
